result.title: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
result.summary: Language models' abilities to interpret tasks and generate programs offer a promising basis for 3D spatial reasoning. Yet following spatial instructions in 3D scenes requires programs to construct geometric references that language leaves implicit. In this work, we introduce VoxProg, which formulates 3D object placement through voxel programming: a language model translates task interpretations into executable programs over local voxel views of scene surfaces. Because these views index surface geometry on regular grids with explicit coordinates and neighborhood relations, an evidence program can isolate task-relevant regions and boundaries directly from scene meshes, and a downstream pose program can measure the resulting geometry to compute a target $SE(3)$ pose. Visual and numerical feedback from execution lets the model inspect intermediate selections and candidate placements to iteratively revise its code. To evaluate open-ended placement across functional use, geometric fit, and contextual arrangements, we introduce the 71-task VoxProg-Bench benchmark along with an evaluation suite pairing perceptual Intent Alignment and 3D Physical Validity. Across VoxProg-Bench and external benchmarks, VoxProg consistently outperforms relation-based, keypoint-based, and mesh-based baselines.

AI.brief_summary: VoxProg 把 3D 物体放置表述为 voxel programming：语言模型将任务解释转成在局部 voxel 视图上可执行的程序，用证据程序从场景网格中选出任务相关区域，再由位姿程序测量几何并算出目标 SE(3) 位姿，并借执行得到的视觉与数值反馈迭代改代码；同时提出 71 任务的 VoxProg-Bench 及 Intent Alignment 与 3D Physical Validity 评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接处理几何与任务必要信息的显式提取和视觉证据筛选，可作为「由 latent 状态承担几何推理」的对照基线，供核查 LVR 中内部表示是否真的必要。
